result.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
result.summary: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either performance or safety with all harnesses scoring between 42.9 (Claude Code) and 45.2 (OpenClaw) for pass@1.

AI.brief_summary: ShellBench 提出 100 个基于真实用户请求的日常任务基准，在含杂乱文件与冲突数据源的工作区中同时评估正确性与安全性，并用 12 个模型、5 种 harness、3 个推理档位共 53,100 次 rollout 比较模型与 harness 的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是纯工具型 agent 的端到端得分与成本对比，不涉及视觉细节表示、latent 推理状态生成或证据筛选与停止决策的内部机制分析，也未给出可供迁移的状态或训练层面线索，故排除。
